newsitem.title: FRANCE: French supreme court backs police chief suspension.
newsitem.headline: French supreme court backs police chief suspension.

text.p: The French supreme court on Wednesday upheld the suspension of a senior police commander for refusing to help an investigating magistrate carry out a raid on the home of Paris mayor Jean Tiberi as part of a corruption probe.

The Cour de Cassation rejected an appeal by Olivier Foll, head of the Paris judicial police, against a six-month suspension imposed by a lower court for ordering his men to refuse a request for assistance by judge Eric Halphen last June.
Tiberi is a close political ally of President Jacques Chirac and succeeded him as mayor of the French capital in 1995.
The magistrate was searching for evidence in a far-reaching investigation into alleged illicit funding of Chirac's Gaullist RPR party through rake-offs on public housing contracts.
The opposition Socialist Party and the left-leaning Magistrates' Union both called for Foll to be suspended following the ruling.
"The Interior Minister (Jean-Louis Debre) must now respect the judicial decision and suspend Olivier Foll immediately," the Socialists said in a statement.
"Debre, who had shown no hesitation in saying that the lower court had made a mistake, went too far," it added.
The lower court ruled that Foll had acted without legal justification, although Interior Minister Jean-Louis Debre publicly supported him and kept him at his post.

In his defence, Foll said he had received no written request for assistance and accused the judge of using "cloak-and-dagger" methods by refusing to tell detectives in advance where they were to raid.
The supreme court ruling said there was no legal need for a written request or for the magistrate to inform the police in advance of the destination.

"A police officer...may not without incurring personal liability refuse to carry out an order given by an investigating magistrate unless he has specifically notified the magistate that an order appears to him to be manifestly illegal," it said.
